identificationModule.briefTitle: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Tolerability of V114 and Prevnar 13™ in Healthy Infants (V114-031/PNEU-LINK)
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Phase 3, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Active Comparator-controlled Study to Evaluate the Safety and Tolerability of V114 in Healthy Infants (PNEU-LINK)

armGroups.label: V114
armGroups.description: Participants will receive a single 0.5 mL intramuscular (IM) injection of V114 at approximately 2 months of age (Vaccination 1); approximately 4 months of age (Vaccination 2); approximately 6 months of age (Vaccination 3); and approximately 12-15 months of age (Vaccination 4).

outcomeMeasures.title: Percentage of Participants With a Solicited Injection-site Adverse Event
outcomeMeasures.description: An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a clinical study participant, temporally associated with the use of study treatment, whether or not considered related to the study treatment. Solicited injection-site AEs included injection-site erythema (redness), injection-site induration (hard lump), injection-site pain (tenderness), and injection-site swelling.
outcomeMeasures.populationDescription: All randomized participants who received at least 1 dose of study vaccination
outcomeMeasures.timeFrame: Up to Day 14 after each study vaccination

outcomeMeasures.title: Percentage of Participants With a Solicited Systemic Adverse Event
outcomeMeasures.description: An AE is any untoward medical occurrence in a clinical study participant, temporally associated with the use of study treatment, whether or not considered related to the study treatment. Solicited systemic AEs included decreased appetite, irritability, somnolence (drowsiness), and urticaria (hives or welts).

outcomeMeasures.title: Percentage of Participants With a Vaccine-related Serious Adverse Event
outcomeMeasures.description: A serious adverse event (SAE) is an AE that results in death, is life-threatening, requires or prolongs an existing hospitalization, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, is a congenital anomaly or birth defect, or is another important medical event deemed such by medical or scientific judgment. SAEs that were reported by the investigator to be at least possibly related to the study vaccination were summarized.

outcomeMeasures.title: Geometric Mean Concentration (GMC) of Serotype-specific Immunoglobulin G (IgG) at 30 Days After Vaccination 3 (Premature Infants Only)
outcomeMeasures.description: The GMC of IgG serotype-specific antibodies to the 13 serotypes (1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F, and 23F) included in V114 and Prevnar 13™ and 2 serotypes (22F and 33F) unique to V114 were quantitated from participants' sera by a multiplex electrochemiluminescence (ECL) assay. This endpoint was part of a Premature Infant Immunogenicity Substudy.
outcomeMeasures.populationDescription: All randomized participants in the Premature Infant Immunogenicity Substudy who did not have protocol deviations that could have substantially affected the results of the immunogenicity analysis and who had sufficient data to perform the analysis for each serotype
outcomeMeasures.timeFrame: 30 days after Vaccination 3 (approximately 5 months after Vaccination 1)

outcomeMeasures.title: Percentage of Participants Meeting Serotype-specific IgG Threshold of ≥0.35 μg/mL 30 Days After Vaccination 3 (Premature Infants Only)
outcomeMeasures.description: The GMC of IgG serotype-specific antibodies to the 13 serotypes (1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F, and 23F) included in V114 and Prevnar 13™ and 2 serotypes (22F and 33F) unique to V114 were quantitated from participants' sera by a multiplex electrochemiluminescence (ECL) assay. Immunoglobulin G for the 15 serotypes contained in V114 vaccine was determined using a pneumococcal electrochemiluminescence (PnECL) assay. This endpoint was part of a Premature Infant Immunogenicity Substudy.

adverseEventsModule.timeFrame: Non-serious AEs: up to 14 days after each vaccination dose; serious AEs and deaths (all causes): up to 6 months after Vaccination 4 (up to 19 months after Vaccination 1)
adverseEventsModule.description:
The safety analysis population included all randomized participants who received at least 1 dose of study vaccination.

The analysis population for All-Cause Mortality included all randomized participants.
